title: Durable, antigen-specific reversal of established autoimmunity

concept.text: The proposed innovation would durably switch off immune responses that cause established autoimmune disease while retaining protective immunity against infections and other unrelated threats. A finite intervention would establish lasting control of harmful self-reactivity, allowing remission without ongoing disease-directed treatment. Antigen specificity would mean selectivity for responses against disease-causing self-antigens. Demonstrating this capability requires evidence that the intervention selectively controls those responses and preserves useful immune function.

Established autoimmunity can involve responses to multiple self-antigens and interactions among immune-cell populations. The supplied CASTLE material documents several autoantibody targets and describes disease mechanisms involving T-cell-mediated B-cell activation, autoantibody production and tissue injury. This makes coordinated control of pathogenic immune responses an important part of the proposed capability.

Proposed scope includes patients whose relevant targets are incompletely identified or change over time. These possibilities remain important uncertainties in the original concept, although the supplied evidence does not establish the assertions about unknown initiating antigens or evolving targets. Avoiding treatment-induced autoimmunity is also a proposed safety requirement whose feasibility remains to be demonstrated.

significance.text: If durable selective tolerance could be achieved across different disease mechanisms, responsive autoimmune conditions could become treatable with a short course followed by sustained remission. Patients could spend prolonged periods without disease-directed immunosuppression while retaining protective immune responses. CASTLE provides a clinical foundation for investigating finite treatment through its report of sustained disease control following a single CAR-T-cell infusion, with no participant requiring reintroduction of immunosuppressants or glucocorticoids during the reported follow-up.

Conditional downstream possibilities include reducing the burden of continuing treatment and limiting additional immune-mediated tissue injury. The magnitude of these benefits would depend on remission durability, treatment toxicity, preservation of immune protection and applicability across diseases. CASTLE studied three pathophysiologically related, B-cell-mediated conditions, leaving broader generalization across mechanistically different autoimmunity open.

Immune disease control and tissue recovery are distinct outcomes. CASTLE describes persistent muscular weakness attributed to longstanding disease in a participant with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, illustrating how residual damage can persist despite improvement in immune disease activity. Restoring destroyed tissue or lost function could require regenerative or rehabilitative advances alongside successful tolerance induction.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is durable, selective control of established disease-causing self-reactivity with preserved protective immunity. Broad CD19-directed B-cell depletion supplies an important clinical approach to disease control. Establishing antigen-specific tolerance additionally requires showing how harmful self-reactive responses are selectively eliminated, restrained or durably reprogrammed, and how that control persists as the immune system reconstitutes.

Scientific and engineering synthesis identifies several concrete barriers. An intervention must identify or functionally isolate the relevant pathogenic responses, address disease sustained by interacting T- and B-cell populations, and cover multiple relevant self-antigens. It must also establish a stable state that resists recurrence after treatment ends. Handling incompletely known or evolving targets is a proposed extension of these requirements, with its relevance and feasibility unresolved by the supplied evidence.

Preservation of protective immunity requires functional evidence. CASTLE reported broadly stable antibody titers to previous vaccinations, alongside a moderate decrease in SARS-CoV-2 titers and a requirement for immunoglobulin substitution in seven patients. Those measurements leave open how well treated patients respond to new vaccine challenges and unrelated infections. Separating persistent antibody levels from broader immune competence is therefore a central measurement challenge.

Proposed development requirements include controlling the risks and burdens of the intervention itself, determining which patients and disease mechanisms are responsive, and monitoring for newly induced autoimmunity. A practical solution would need a treatment burden and safety profile justified by its durable benefit. These requirements extend beyond the clinical and mechanistic conclusions established by the supplied study.

current_state.text: Müller and colleagues published the phase 1/2 CASTLE basket trial, “CD19 CAR-T cells for treatment-refractory autoimmune diseases,” on 7 January 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41591-025-04185-6. The study enrolled 24 participants with systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis or idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. At 24 weeks, 22 participants achieved their disease-specific predefined efficacy endpoints. The endpoints comprised remission, non-progression or moderate/major response, depending on the disease, so the aggregate count represents several different forms of clinical benefit.

Treatment involved cyclophosphamide/fludarabine lymphodepleting chemotherapy followed by a single infusion of CD19-directed CAR-T cells. B cells were rapidly depleted in all participants. CD19 supplies a B-cell-lineage target, while the proposed innovation requires selectivity for disease-causing self-reactivity. The reported clinical improvements and autoantibody reductions establish a foundation for investigating immune resetting, with antigen-specific tolerance remaining an open mechanistic question.

Reported follow-up had a median duration of 13 months and a maximum of 23 months. No participant required reintroduction of immunosuppressants or glucocorticoids during that follow-up. These observations support sustained disease control within the reported period. The small cohort and absence of a control arm limit causal attribution and comparative assessment, while the duration leaves longer-term relapse risk and permanent remission unresolved.

Autoantibodies against nucleosomes, histones and Smith antigen decreased and became negative in most patients, providing evidence of changes in several self-reactive antibody responses. Antibody titers to previous vaccinations generally remained stable, with the qualifications concerning SARS-CoV-2 titers and immunoglobulin substitution described above. Establishing selective tolerance and comprehensive protective immunity would require additional cellular, mechanistic and functional measurements.

The supplied review reports that saved full article HTML and PDF text support these findings, resolving the earlier publisher-access limitation. The results are author-reported outcomes assessed through that review. Figure images were outside its visual inspection, and the associated protocol supplement was available through an extraction truncated at PDF page 63. Protocol background supports the described immune-cell interactions, with the extraction boundary limiting conclusions about material beyond that point.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration would consist of controlled trials across mechanistically different autoimmune diseases showing multi-year remission without ongoing disease-directed treatment. Each disease would need explicit clinical and organ-specific endpoints, documented baseline severity and continued observation for relapse. Multi-year duration and cross-mechanism breadth are proposed completion criteria for this record. Finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth within the populations and conditions studied.
completion_criteria.label: Multi-year treatment-free remission across mechanistically different autoimmune diseases

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mechanistic demonstration would show durable, selective control of relevant self-reactive cells and responses, alongside measurements of clinical benefit. Longitudinal assessment should connect changes in pathogenic T- and B-cell activity, relevant autoantibodies and immune reconstitution to continued remission. Evidence should establish disease-antigen selectivity and explain how broad depletion, where used, leads to the subsequent immune state.
completion_criteria.label: Durable antigen-selective control of self-reactivity linked to clinical remission

completion_criteria.text: Proposed preservation-of-immunity testing would evaluate functional responses to unrelated vaccines and infections, with attention to both retained immune memory and responses to new challenges. Interpretation should account for immunoglobulin replacement and other supportive treatment that could affect antibody measurements. Long-term follow-up should assess new autoimmunity and clinically important treatment-related harm alongside remission.
completion_criteria.label: Functional immunity to unrelated vaccines and infections remains preserved

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries include confirmation in independent cohorts and treatment centers, transparent reporting of failures and relapses, and evidence that outcomes can be reproduced with consistently manufactured and administered treatment. Studies should define which patient groups, disease mechanisms and stages of tissue damage are covered. Testing patients with multiple or evolving targets would address the proposed breadth requirement, while documenting immune control and residual organ impairment as separate outcomes.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible outcomes across independent cohorts and centers with defined boundaries

related_concepts.text: Conceptual synthesis links IMM-04 to IMM-01, “A general decoder for T-cell antigen recognition,” and IMM-02, “A predictive, causal theory of whole immune responses.” Decoding recognition could help identify relevant self-reactive T cells, while causal immune models could help explain how selective intervention produces a durable system-wide state. IMM-04 has a therapeutic endpoint in established autoimmune disease. IMM-11, “Causal mechanisms that initiate the breakdown of self-tolerance,” addresses disease initiation and could inform that treatment even when the initiating event preceded the established disease by years.

Conceptual synthesis identifies a close relationship with IMM-05, “Routine donor-specific transplant tolerance without lifelong immunosuppression.” Both seek durable antigen-selective tolerance with preserved protective immunity. IMM-04 concerns harmful responses against the patient's own tissues, while IMM-05 concerns responses against donor tissue. Their target contexts and clinical completion demonstrations remain distinct.

Conceptual synthesis connects IMM-04 with IMM-03, “Vaccine design that reliably directs broadly protective antibody evolution,” through selective control of adaptive immunity. IMM-03 seeks to build protective antibody responses, while IMM-04 seeks to restrain harmful self-reactivity. IMM-06, “General immune eradication of heterogeneous solid tumors,” and IMM-07, “Immune-mediated, treatment-free control of established HIV infection,” likewise share interests in specificity and durable immune effects, with disease-specific goals involving tumor eradication and control of persistent infection.

Conceptual synthesis links IMM-08, “Restoration of youthful immune competence in older adults,” to the protective-immunity dimension of IMM-04. Restoration of age-impaired immune function and selective tolerance in autoimmunity require different demonstrations. IMM-12, “Programmable trained immunity with predictable protection and safety,” concerns programmable innate immune memory and could interact with adaptive disease control, while retaining a separate mechanistic focus.

Conceptual synthesis places IMM-09, “In-body programming of immune cells as an inexpensive, scalable treatment,” alongside IMM-04 as a possible enabling delivery and manufacturing capability. An in-body programming platform could potentially implement a tolerance-inducing intervention, subject to evidence of specificity, durability and safety. IMM-10, “Real-time immune control of life-threatening systemic inflammation,” shares the goal of controlling harmful immune activity, with its completion centered on acute systemic control and IMM-04 centered on lasting control of established self-reactivity.

Conceptual synthesis connects IMM-13, “Predictive causal control of microbiome–immune interactions,” and IMM-14, “Causal, bidirectional control of neuroimmune circuits,” as possible routes for understanding or influencing immune regulation. Either could contribute to autoimmune treatment if causal effects on pathogenic self-reactivity were established. Their broader microbiome and neuroimmune capabilities retain separate identities, and the supplied CASTLE evidence leaves their contribution to durable antigen-specific tolerance unresolved.

change_log.change: Preserved IMM-04 and its original title while defining antigen specificity in terms of disease-causing self-reactivity.
change_log.reason: The review distinguishes disease-antigen-specific tolerance from recognition of a broad lineage marker such as CD19.

change_log.change: Expanded the clinical result to identify all three diseases, the heterogeneous 24-week efficacy endpoints, and median and maximum follow-up.
change_log.reason: The 22-of-24 aggregate includes remission, non-progression and moderate/major response. Its interpretation depends on endpoint and follow-up scope.

change_log.change: Integrated lymphodepletion, rapid broad B-cell depletion and the absence of a control arm into the clinical interpretation.
change_log.reason: These features determine what the study can establish about treatment effects and selective tolerance.

change_log.change: Removed the obsolete publisher-access qualification and retained the review's actual inspection and extraction boundaries.
change_log.reason: The supplied review reports complete saved article text, while figure images were outside visual inspection and the protocol supplement extraction was truncated.

change_log.change: Retained unknown initiating antigens, evolving targets and avoidance of new autoimmunity as qualified scope uncertainties and proposed requirements.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence leaves these assertions unresolved. Preserving them with explicit qualification maintains the concept without overstating its evidentiary foundation.

change_log.change: Integrated autoantibody findings, vaccination-titer observations, the SARS-CoV-2 qualification and immunoglobulin substitution in seven patients.
change_log.reason: These details support the immune-preservation discussion while clarifying the additional functional evidence required.

change_log.change: Separated durable immune control from recovery of damaged tissue and made broader disease applicability conditional.
change_log.reason: Residual muscular weakness illustrates the tissue-recovery boundary, and three related B-cell-mediated diseases provide limited evidence of cross-mechanism generalization.

change_log.change: Developed explicitly proposed clinical, mechanistic, functional and reproducibility criteria.
change_log.reason: The requested capability requires evidence beyond clinical response alone, and the proposed thresholds carry no claim of established consensus.

change_log.change: Added relationships to every other supplied roster entry as labeled conceptual synthesis.
change_log.reason: This preserves the roster's separate identities while explaining relevant overlap without attributing those relationships to the CASTLE study.

unresolved_issues: The supplied freshness record is empty. Coverage of developments through 2026-11-01 remains unassessed, and the supplied material cannot establish the latest state of the field.
The extent to which unknown initiating antigens or evolving targets constrain treatment remains unresolved by the supplied evidence.
The mechanism and durability of disease-antigen-specific tolerance after broad B-cell depletion remain open, including the relationship between immune reconstitution and relapse.
Functional protection against unrelated infections and new vaccine challenges remains insufficiently established by the reported preexisting antibody measurements.
Long-term remission beyond the reported maximum follow-up of 23 months, comparative efficacy and applicability across mechanistically different autoimmune diseases remain unresolved.
The feasibility of preventing newly induced autoimmunity and achieving an acceptable long-term treatment burden remains to be demonstrated.
The supplied review's truncated protocol extraction and absence of visual figure inspection limit conclusions requiring those materials.

brief.title: Lasting relief from the immune system attacking the body
possible: People with autoimmune disease, in which the immune system attacks the body, could receive a short course of treatment and stay well without continuing disease treatment. It would stop harmful attacks while preserving defenses against infections.
why: Patients could spend prolonged periods free from medicines that suppress immunity. Lasting control could also prevent further damage to organs and tissues.

sources.showed: In CASTLE, 24 patients received chemotherapy and engineered immune cells that remove B cells, a type of immune cell. Most met disease-specific goals ranging from remission to halted progression. None restarted immune-suppressing medicines during follow-up.
sources.quote: B cells were rapidly depleted in all patients
sources.cited_for: CASTLE supports sustained disease control after a finite treatment.
sources.not_established: The small trial lacked a control group and did not establish lasting, selective control of harmful immune responses.

sources.who: Fabian Müller, Jule Taubmann and colleagues
sources.showed: An earlier case series treated 15 patients with engineered immune cells after chemotherapy. Disease measures improved, and all stopped immune-suppressing treatment.
sources.quote:
Immunosuppressive therapy was completely stopped in all 
the patients.
sources.cited_for: The case series supports the possibility of disease control without continuing immune suppression.
sources.not_established: An uncontrolled case series cannot establish comparative benefit or reliable long-term remission.

sources.who: Jinmin Lee and colleagues, University of Pennsylvania
sources.showed: Engineered immune cells selectively killed patient B cells making antibodies against a disease target. In a preclinical model of pemphigus, a blistering disease, treatment resolved blisters.
sources.quote: Toxicology screens using primary human cells and high-throughput membrane proteome arrays did not identify off-target cytotoxic interactions.
sources.cited_for: The work supports selective removal of immune cells attacking a particular target in the body.
sources.not_established: Preclinical results do not establish durable remission or preserved protective immunity in people.

sources.who: Mohammad Alhadj Ali, Yuk-Fun Liu, Danijela Tatovic and colleagues
sources.showed: People with newly diagnosed diabetes received a fragment of proinsulin, a precursor of insulin. Treated groups maintained daily insulin use while the placebo group needed more.
sources.quote: Treatment was well tolerated with no systemic or local hypersensitivity.
sources.cited_for: The study links treatment directed at a disease-related target with changes in immune responses and insulin reserve.
sources.not_established: It did not demonstrate treatment-free remission or reversal of longstanding disease.

sources.showed: Researchers measured antibodies against the body's own proteins. Each person's pattern stayed stable over years. Treatments targeting antibody-producing plasma cells changed these patterns much more than some other B-cell treatments.
sources.quote: For each individual, the set of resulting autoreactivites constituted a unique immunological fingerprint, or “autoreactome,” that was remarkably stable over years.
sources.cited_for: Broad antibody measurements can reveal harmful responses that may persist after treatment.
sources.not_established: Changing an antibody pattern does not establish selective control of disease or lasting clinical remission.

shown: Müller and colleagues have demonstrated sustained disease control after broad B-cell removal. CASTLE followed patients for up to 23 months. Its outcomes included remission, halted progression and improvement, depending on the disease.

Lee and colleagues demonstrated more selective targeting in preclinical experiments. Together, these approaches show parts of the goal, but lasting selective control with preserved immune protection has yet to be demonstrated.
missing: Controlled trials have yet to establish years of treatment-free remission across diseases driven by different immune mechanisms.
Selective control of harmful immune responses must persist as immune cells return after treatment.
Protection against infections and responses to new vaccines must remain functional without relying on replacement antibodies.

milestones.label: Years without treatment across different autoimmune diseases
milestones.explanation: Controlled trials would have to show multi-year remission across diseases with different immune mechanisms, using clear disease and organ measures. This would establish lasting clinical benefit and its breadth.

milestones.label: Lasting control of responses against disease targets
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to link remission to selective control of harmful immune cells and antibodies as the immune system rebuilds. This would establish why disease stays controlled.

milestones.label: Immune protection remains intact
milestones.explanation: Testing would have to show retained immune memory and responses to new vaccines and infections, accounting for supportive treatment and tracking harm. This would establish that protection survives disease control.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce results and define who benefits
milestones.explanation: Independent cohorts and centers would have to reproduce outcomes with consistent treatment, reporting failures, relapses and residual damage. This would define which patients and disease mechanisms benefit.

uncertain: It remains unclear whether treatment can cover disease targets that are incompletely known or change over time.
The long-term treatment burden and risk of triggering new autoimmune disease remain unresolved.
Stopping immune attacks may leave permanent tissue damage that needs separate treatment.
